title: Replication Timing
summary: Replicated content arrives on clients AFTER the server creates it — sometimes milliseconds, sometimes seconds later. Client code that assumes instant availability races ahead of reality. WaitForChild and event-driven code fix it.

explanation.whatItIs: The network gap between 'server created it' and 'client has it'. Every LocalScript starts racing against arrivals it can't see.
explanation.whyItExists: Replication rides network packets scheduled by the engine — not guaranteed synchronous with your script startup.
whenToUse: WaitForChild with timeout for expected-but-delayed content
Structuring: server signals readiness via a RemoteEvent instead of clients polling
whenNotToUse: Sleeping arbitrary seconds 'to be safe' — race windows vary; use waits/events
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
t=0   server: creates Folder "Shop"
t=12ms server: packet queued
t=??ms client: packet arrives  ← only NOW can client code see it

Client script started at t=0 and looked at t=1ms:
  FindFirstChild → nil. (It wasn't late. YOU were early.)
```
tips: Anything in ReplicatedStorage that a LocalScript needs: WaitForChild
For streaming-enabled games, treat far-away content as possibly GONE too
commonMistakes: LocalScript indexing ReplicatedStorage children directly at startup
No timeout on WaitForChild → silent infinite yield when names mismatch
Caching replicated objects that streaming later removes

examples.title: Robust client access
examples.code:
-- ❌ racy:
-- local shop = ReplicatedStorage.Shop

-- ✅ waits:
local shop = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Shop", 10)
assert(shop, "Shop folder missing — check replication")

-- ✅ open-ended arrivals:
ReplicatedStorage.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child)
    print("Newly replicated:", child:GetFullName())
end)
